repo_reality_notes: Current master carries helper-first Zig segments under tools/lib/bpf/zigux_segments.

Current master now carries tools/lib/bpf/zigux_segments/file_path_handle_bridge.zig for helper-only proc-fdinfo pathname shaping, compact fdinfo map-info parsing, reused-map compatibility summaries, pinned-map reuse planning, and planning-only token readiness while direct procfs reads, bpffs opens, and descriptor ownership still stay deferred.

Current master also carries ready-buffer helper shards that split ready-attempt-to-fd lookup and ready-attempt-to-window lookup into stable-output review surfaces under tools/lib/bpf/zigux_segments/ready_buffer_fd_lookup.zig and tools/lib/bpf/zigux_segments/perf_buffer_ready_window.zig.

segments.why_now: This slice is mostly string tables, log-level gating, and version reporting, so it gives Zigux a low-risk libbpf foothold with stable output semantics.
Path concatenation and bpffs-style pin-name sanitization are bounded helpers that can be validated without entering mkdir, statfs, unlink, or verifier-facing behavior.
The CPU mask parser is self-contained text processing that future perf-buffer and feature probes can share, which makes it a good first real port after the survey scaffold.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: exported attach, link, map, and program type string tables
segments.why_now: The exported enum-to-name tables are dense lookups with stable output behavior, so they extend the helper-first libbpf foothold without widening into object loading, verifier work, or syscall-backed state.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: bpf_get_map_info_from_fdinfo() pathname and fdinfo text parsing
segments.why_now: The shared file-path bridge destination already carries the bounded procfs path construction and fdinfo text parsing helpers, so this landed slice should stay explicitly smaller than direct file reads, descriptor ownership, or pinned-object reopen flow.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: bpf_map__reuse_fd() name selection and bpf_object__reuse_map() compatibility checks
segments.why_now: The shared bridge surface now already carries the reused-map-name chooser and compatibility comparison as landed helper-only behavior, and it should stay reviewable without widening into FD duplication, close-on-replacement, or pinned-map reopen side effects.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: bpf_object_prepare_token() and bpf_object__reuse_map() handle-bridging paths
segments.why_now: This remaining file-path and handle bridge still crosses real procfs reads, bpffs opens, token creation, bpf_obj_get() reopen flow, and fd ownership semantics, so the helper-first packet should keep it deferred.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: perf_buffer__new() online-CPU routing and perf_event setup
segments.why_now: The broader online-CPU routing path still combines sysfs reads, perf_event_open setup, mmap-backed ring state, map updates, epoll registration, and timeout-sensitive polling, but current master already carries the bounded online-CPU cursor and routing-summary helper in online_cpu_routing.zig, so the setup-side packet stays deferred without pretending that helper-local routing evidence is absent.
This remains the nearest post-helper cluster, but it depends on bpf_object, bpf_map, and bpf_program model parity that the repo has not started yet.

The object-model and ELF collection surface is where mirror-tree sprawl becomes likely, so it should stay deferred until the smaller helper-first segments and the nearer skeleton blocker are fully settled.

BTF fixups, extern resolution, relocation recording, and load-time verifier interactions remain the densest libbpf surface and still need the smaller helper-first and object-model boundaries to stay explicit ahead of them.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: perf_buffer__poll() wait-result classification and ordered process_records bookkeeping
segments.why_now: The bounded poll-summary helper proves wait-result normalization and ready-buffer accounting without widening into epoll wiring, mmap-backed ring ownership, or online-CPU setup.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: reused-map name retention before compatibility comparison
segments.why_now: This materializes the shared bridge destination with side-effect-free pathname shaping and bounded reused-map name retention while leaving direct procfs reads, live bpffs opens, token materialization, `bpf_obj_get()` reopen flow, and descriptor ownership side effects to the deferred file-path-and-handle bridge boundary.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: perf_buffer__poll() ready buffer descriptor lookup after ready-attempt selection
segments.why_now: The dedicated ready-buffer fd lookup helper keeps slot-to-ready-attempt translation and errno-shaped fd lookup outputs stable without widening into epoll wiring, perf_event setup, or ring ownership behavior.

anchor_ranges: tools/lib/bpf/libbpf.c: perf_buffer__poll() ready buffer mapped-window lookup around process_records bookkeeping
segments.why_now: The ready-buffer window helper isolates mapped-size and lookup-return summaries for already-ready buffers, extending stable-output poll bookkeeping without widening into mmap ownership, ring lifecycle, or wait orchestration.
